Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

City Council thanked Social Services, and all supporting departments involved in making
the Social Services 50th Anniversary Celebration events a success. Vice Mayor Ayala
thanked Gabriela Regalado, Social Services Director, and Levy Sun, Director of
Communications and Public Affairs, for the success of all the Social Services 50th
Anniversary events. Councilmember Perez welcomed all in attendance; highlighted the
Social Services building remodel; reminded everyone of the upcoming election;
encouraged residents to look after their neighbors; thanked Chamber of Commerce for
kicking off Breast Cancer Awareness Month; and shared that she will be absent at the
next City Council Meeting. Councilmember Valencia reported on her attendance at
Norwalk High School’s Candidate Meet and Greet, the Chamber of Commerce
Candidates Forum, and Social Services 50th Anniversary Celebration; and announced the
Norwalk Lions Club is hosting a Pancake Breakfast Fundraiser October 6 at the Norwalk
Arts and Sports Complex. Councilmember Ramirez shared that he has a few extra tickets
available for the Norwalk Lions Club pancake breakfast. Mayor Rios reported on her
attendance at the Mayor’s Clergy Meeting, Sanchez Elementary College and Career Day,
Give Back to National Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate
Programs Fundraising Event, free movie screening at Milagro Cinemas, Paint the Town
Pink Kickoff, McDonalds Restaurant Digital Re-Grand Opening, and Social Services 50th
Anniversary Celebration; and announced she also has tickets available for the Lions Club
Pancake Breakfast Fundraiser.

Safety Emergency Management Team.

Norwalk.

  NORWALK TANK FARM

Background:

The City received a request from the Water Replenishment District (WRD) for a Non-
Consumptive Water Use Permit (NCWUP) related to their groundwater cleanup program. The
WRD has the authority to issue pumping right exemptions under a NCWUP to water purveyors
in the Central Basin for groundwater treatment programs that remedy groundwater
contamination and do not put the treated water to beneficial use. Groundwater pumped under a
NCWUP will not count against the City’s water rights. This authority is described in Section
II1.B.7 of the Central Basin Third Amended Judgment (Judgment).

The former Defense Fuel Support Point – Norwalk, also called the Norwalk Tank Farm (Site) is
located at 15306 Norwalk Boulevard. Aboveground storage tanks were previously used at the
site to store and distribute jet fuel to military installations in the western United States. Santa Fe
Pacific Pipeline, L.P. (SFPP), a subsidiary of Kinder Morgan, Inc. leases an easement on the
Site that includes pipelines for conveying fuels. Under the clean-up orders and oversight of the
Los Angeles Regional Water Quality Control Board, the United States Defense Logistics Agency
- Energy (DLA-Energy) and SFPP have been performing ongoing environmental remediation at
the Site which includes remediation and treatment of contaminated groundwater and soil. The
primary chemicals of concern at the Site include petroleum hydrocarbons (fuel products),
benzene, methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE), tertiary butyl alcohol (TBA), and 1,2-dichloroethane
(1,2-DCA).
 City Council  October 15, 2024
Resolution No. 24-53 – Non-Consumptive Water Use Permit  Page No. 2

In June 2019, the WRD Board of Directors granted a NCWUP (Resolution No. 19-1098) for
assignment to DLA-Energy by the City for the extraction of up to 14 acre-feet per year by DLA-
Energy for remediation at the Site. The 5-year term of the NCWUP (Resolution No. 19-1098)
expired on February 2, 2024. WRD received an application for a renewal NCWUP from Apex
Companies on behalf of DLA-Energy in April 2024 to continue their remediation activities.

The City is not a responsible party, partner, or participant in the clean-up effort by DLA-
Energy. However, since DLA-Energy is not a party to the Judgment, a party needs to petition
for the NCWUP and then assign it to DLA-Energy. The City is a party with water rights in the
Central Basin and has previously entered into agreements and assigned the NCWUP to DLA-
Energy. This has allowed DLA-Energy to extract groundwater for their remediation project. If
approved by City Council, the WRD Board will adopt a resolution to issue a pumping rights
exemption.

The renewed NCWUP would be granted for an additional five years with pumping not to exceed
57.5 acre feet for the five-year period (11.5 acre feet per year). The conditions of this project are
consistent with the criteria outlined in Section 111.B.7 of the Judgment, City Resolution No. 24-
53, agreement for assignment of NCWUP, and a forthcoming WRD resolution (Resolution No.
24-1228).

Background:

In 1992 and 1996, Los Angeles County voters approved two local parks funding measures called
Proposition A. The 1992 Proposition A created the Regional Park and Open Space District

grant funds for more than 1,500 projects for parks, recreational, cultural, and community
facilities, beaches, and open spaces throughout the county.

The Safe, Clean Neighborhood Parks, Open Space Beaches, Rivers Protection, and Water
Conservation Measure, or Measure A, was developed to meet current and future park needs
throughout the County of Los Angeles. A Countywide Parks and Recreation Needs Assessment
was completed in 2015, and the ballot measure was approved by voters in 2016, including
formula-based allocations to agencies throughout the study area and competitive grants open
to public agencies, non-profit organizations, and schools. In order to apply for and accept
Measure A funds, RPOSD requires a resolution from the City of Norwalk. Staff has prepared for
consideration Resolution No, 24-54 authorizing the City to submit grant applications for Measure
A funding. An agreement is also required, which has been prepared and attached.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE EMERGENCY WORK FOR CECILIA STREET SPEED HUMP
  INSTALLATION - PROJECT NO. 7872 - TRANSPORTATION CENTER AND
  SOCIAL SERVICES PARKING LOT RESURFACING

Background:

On June 18, 2024, City Council awarded a contract in the amount of $395,021 to All American
Asphalt (AAA) for Project No. 7872, Transportation Center and Social Services Parking Lots
Resurfacing. The project rehabilitated parking lots at the City’s Transportation Center, the Social
Services Center, and Alondra Library. Work scope includes for pavement surface preparation,
specific location pavement repairs, pavement resurfacing, and pavement markings restoration.
All above work has been satisfactorily completed as of September 19, 2024.

At its’ regularly scheduled August 6, 2024, meeting, City Council approved the installation of
speed hump(s) and associated equipment for Cecilia Street between Orr and Day Road and
Fairford Avenue. The installation of the speed humps is to increase safety, heighten driver
awareness and provide a safer driving experience.

As mentioned in August, with the I-5 freeway improvements completed, more vehicle volume is
being experienced upon the freeway. This itself creates a scenario of “cut-through” traffic, which
is as freeway traffic becomes more congested, drivers are seeking alternate routes to their
destinations. These alternate routes typically traverse through residential streets that are
adjacent to the freeway to get around the freeway congestion and then routed back onto the
freeway. The cut-through traffic typically occurs during rush hours of a working day. The drivers
are typically in a hurry and driving at higher than posted speed limits.
 City Council  October 15, 2024
Project No. 7872 – Approve Emergency Work for Cecilia Street  Page No. 2
Speed Hump Installation

To quicken the installation of speed humps and associated equipment sooner, staff utilized the
subject project contractor to procure the speed hump materials, prepare the roadway surface
and install the speed humps and appurtenances on Cecilia Street. Logistics were involved for
speed humps materials delivery and was considered to affect a better work schedule to complete
the speed hump installation sooner. The estimated costs for the above-described work
(materials, labor & inspection) is $140,000.

Speed hump materials have a typical four-to-six-week delivery time from order placement.
Pavement resurfacing (slurry seal) requires advance preparation work (herbicide spraying, crack
seal) prior to slurry seal application, then followed by pavement marking restoration. Work will
be coordinated such that pavement resurface work will occur in advance of speed hump delivery.
This ensures the slurry seal has adequate time to set. Estimated time for pavement resurface
and speed hump installation to complete is four-to-six weeks by mid November 2024 or sooner.

Gas Tax funds have been identified as available and eligible funding source for this work.

Background:

On October 2, 2018, the City adopted an Economic Development Opportunities Plan that
identified various areas throughout the City that could promote economic development. The site
is a key node identified for its redevelopment potential given its location, size, and access to
transportation. In addition, the plan was updated October 17, 2023.

This City staff-initiated project, involves a 32.3-acre site with a general plan land use designation
and zoning of Institutional (I). The project site is generally situated between Imperial Highway to
the north, the Union Pacific Railroad to the east, and Bloomfield Avenue to the west. The project
site (Assessor’s Parcel Number [APN] 8045-008-902) is located within a predominantly
residential area, with a residential townhome community to the north (Norwalk Manor); a 9.4-
acre public park (Zimmerman Park) to the east; single-family residential units, a senior residential
community, and a hospital (Norwalk Community Hospital) to the south; and single-family
residential units to the west, across Bloomfield Avenue. Regional access to the site is provided
via Interstate 5 (I-5). Local access is provided via Imperial Highway and Bloomfield Avenue.
Additionally, transit access is available for the project site via the Norwalk-Santa Fe Springs
Metrolink Station, located approximately 0.2 miles north of the project site.

The project site was originally developed in 1943 as an all-male youth correctional facility
operated by the California Youth Authority (CYA), which is now known as the California Division

The Specific Plan would guide the development of a mixed-use transit-oriented development.
Transit-oriented development is a compact, walkable, mixed-use residential and commercial
area located within 0.25- to 0.5-miles of a transit station, incorporating features to encourage
transit use throughout the day such as a mix of uses, high-quality pedestrian and bicycle access,
narrow streets, and tailored parking requirements. The proposed Specific Plan includes land use
types such as residential, restaurant, retail service uses, hotel, and ground floor active
commercial/quasi-public spaces and would support transit access.

The Specific Plan is intended to ensure an orderly and efficient development of the project site,
in accordance with the provisions of the City of Norwalk General Plan (General Plan). The
Specific Plan would serve both planning and regulatory functions by providing land use
regulations, identifying site circulation, public facilities/infrastructure, and applicable
development standards and guidelines. All future development within the Specific Plan would be
subject to compliance with the Specific Plan regulations, as well as other applicable Norwalk
Municipal Code (NMC) regulations.

Greenhouse Gas Emissions. With the incorporation of mitigation measures, the identified
potentially significant environmental impacts would be reduced to less than significant levels,
with the one exception of greenhouse gas emissions, as discussed above.

Based on the analysis in this report, Planning Commission and staff are supportive of General

screening thresholds. With the incorporation of mitigation measures, all other potentially
significant environmental impacts can be reduced to less than significant levels. Should the City

development project. Infill development is an important planning principle considering the option

 Institutional (I). 1he project site is generally situated between Imperial Highway to the

 project site (Assessor's Parcel Number [APN] 8045-008-902) is located within a
 predominantly residential area, with a residential townhome community to the north

 The project site was originally developed in 1943 as an all-male youth correctional facility
 operated by the CYA. The CYA (now known as the California Division of Juvenile Justice
 [DJJ]) is a division of the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation that
 provides education and trauma informed treatment to California's youthful offenders up
 to the age of 25 who have the most serious criminal backgrounds and most intense
 treatment needs. As such, the Norwalk CYA facility provided academic and vocational
 education, medical care, and treatment programs, as well as substance abuse and mental
 health needs to inmates. In 2011, the CYA facility operations ceased, and the project site
 remained vacant until 2019, at which time the facility was temporarily utilized by the
 California Department of State Hospitals (DSH) due to the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-
 19) pandemic.

 The project site was being used by the DSH as a temporary satellite mental hospital
 facility to mitigate the effects of "surge space" at local state hospitals until early 2022. The
 facility was housing primarily COVID-negative mental forensic inmates; however, all
 inmates have been moved out of the facility. Currently, the DSH has an agreement with
 the Department of General Services (DGS), who currently owns the property, to use the

 emissions. The project would generate an increase in GHG emissions, either directly or
 indirectly, that would have a significant impact on the environment despite implementation
 of Mitigation Measures GHG 1 through GHG-4. If the City of Norwalk decides to approve
 the project, the City must cite their findings in accordance with Section 15091 of CEQA
 and prepare a Statement of Overriding Considerations in accordance with Section 15093
 of CEQA.

 SUMMARY

 Based on the analysis in this report, staff is supportive of General Plan Amendment No.
 2024-01, Zone Change No. 2024-02, Zoning Text Amendment 2024-04, Specific Plan 17,

 analyzed by the EIR, which finds that one significant and unavoidable impact related to
 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions would result from implementation of the project. It's
